turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope it's okay that I'm here, I don't want to waste your time or anything. 

But... I guess I've just been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. I work in meat processing, and... well, it's kind of embarrassing to admit. I keep starting my tasks, like the sanitation steps, the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork... and I really do try to do a good job, I promise. But somehow, I just keep leaving out the very last parts of them. 

It makes me feel awful because I know my job depends on finishing everything correctly, but I just keep messing that up. Does that... does that make sense? Is that something you might be able to help me with?

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient explicitly states they keep starting tasks at work (sanitation steps, batch logs, paperwork) but fail to finish the last parts of them, which matches difficulty following through on instructions and finishing workplace duties.

turns.doctor_question: When you find yourself unable to finish those last parts of your tasks, is it because you feel a strong, repetitive urge to redo the earlier steps over and over again, or is it more that you feel the work isn't 'perfect' enough to be considered complete?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... no, it's not really like that. I don't think I feel a strong urge to redo things, and it's definitely not because I'm trying to make it perfect. I wish I was that detail-oriented! 

It's more like... I just sort of... drift off, I guess? Like, I'll be almost done, and then my brain just kind of moves on to the next thing before my hands are actually finished with the first thing. I don't mean to do it, I really don't. It's just that the very last step just... slips away from me. 

Is that... is that a bad thing? I mean, I know it's bad for my job, but does that sound like something you've heard before? I hope I'm explaining it right.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient describes failing to finish tasks, stating that 'the very last step just slips away from me.'
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient explains that they 'drift off' and their 'brain just kind of moves on to the next thing,' indicating distractibility by unrelated thoughts.
symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly denies that their inability to finish tasks is due to perfectionism or trying to make the work perfect.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly denies feeling a strong, repetitive urge to redo things.

turns.doctor_question: Does this tendency to drift off or lose track of the final steps happen in other areas of your life, like with chores at home or personal errands, or is it strictly happening at work?
turns.patient_response:
Um, I guess it's mostly just work? I mean, I try really hard to keep on top of everything at home, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just lazy or living in a mess or anything like that. 

I... well, maybe sometimes I'll start folding laundry and then remember I need to start the dishwasher, so the laundry might sit there for a little bit. But I always mean to go back to it! It's not like I'm completely ignoring my responsibilities. Everyone gets a little sidetracked sometimes, right? 

I'm really trying my best to keep everything together. I hope that's an okay answer... does that sound normal to you?

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient admits to starting chores like folding laundry but leaving them unfinished to do something else.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes getting sidetracked from tasks by unrelated thoughts, such as remembering to start the dishwasher while folding laundry.
symptom_reasoning.S042: The patient displays a lack of self-assurance and fear of negative evaluation, repeatedly seeking validation ('I hope that's an okay answer... does that sound normal to you?').

turns.doctor_question: Aside from these struggles with your tasks, have you been feeling persistently sad, empty, or lost interest in activities you usually enjoy over the past few weeks?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no, definitely not. Um, I really don't feel sad or empty at all. I mean, it's a little frustrating when I mess up at work, of course, because I really want to do a good job for my boss, but it doesn't make me depressed or anything. 

I still really enjoy my days off and doing things I like. I try really hard to stay positive and upbeat, I promise. I'm actually a pretty happy person overall! 

I hope that's okay? Like, I hope I'm not supposed to be feeling sad for you to be able to help me. I just want to fix this little work issue so I can be a better employee. Is that a helpful answer?

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly states they do not feel sad or empty at all and consider themselves a happy person.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly denies losing interest, stating they still really enjoy their days off and doing things they like.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back at your childhood, say when you were in elementary school, did you often have similar difficulties with staying focused on tasks or finishing your schoolwork?
turns.patient_response:
Um, well, I guess maybe a little bit? I really don't want you to think I was a bad student, because I promise I wasn't! I actually understood the lessons really well. But, um, my mom actually still has some of my old report cards, like from around fourth grade, and... well, the teachers always wrote that I was really bright, which is a good thing, right? 

But they also usually said that I needed, um, constant reminders to finish my classwork and actually turn my homework in. It wasn't that I was being defiant or anything! I just... I would somehow miss chunks of the instructions unless the teacher was standing right close to me. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was just ignoring them on purpose. I really did try to be a good student and make my teachers happy. Does that... is that the kind of thing you were looking for?

symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient reports missing chunks of instructions unless the teacher was standing right next to them, indicating difficulty listening when spoken to.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient explicitly mentions needing constant reminders to finish classwork and turn in homework during elementary school.

turns.doctor_question: When you were in school or even now in your daily life, do you often find it difficult to stay seated or feel a need to be constantly moving around?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no, definitely not. Um, I'm actually really good at staying in one place, I promise. I don't feel restless or like I need to be running around at all. Even at work, I just stay right at my station where I'm supposed to be and do my job. 

I was never one of those kids who bounced off the walls or disrupted class, either... I always tried my best to be quiet and polite so I wouldn't bother the teachers. 

I hope that's okay? Like, I hope it doesn't mean I'm wasting your time if I don't have that specific problem. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me. Is it normal to just struggle with the focusing part but be totally fine sitting still?

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient mentions that they 'struggle with the focusing part'.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states they are good at staying in one place and stay at their station at work.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly denies feeling restless or needing to run around.
symptom_reasoning.S013: The patient notes they always tried to be quiet and polite, denying difficulty engaging in activities quietly.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient denies being a kid who 'bounced off the walls', indicating no constant, motor-like activity.
